skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development

skills.name: troubleshooting

skills.name: user-app-development

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. //==================================================================================================
5. // Imports
6. //==================================================================================================
7. 
8. use vstd::prelude::*;
9. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
10. include!("upool.spec.rs");
11. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
12. include!("upool.proof.rs");
13. 
14. use crate::{
15.     hal::mem::FrameAddress,
16.     mm::phys::frame,
17. };
18. use ::core::mem::ManuallyDrop;
19. use ::sys::error::Error;
20. 
21. //==================================================================================================
22. // User Frame
23. //==================================================================================================
24. 
25. ///
26. /// # Description
27. ///
28. /// A type that represents a user frame.
29. ///
30. #[derive(Debug)]
31. #[verus_verify(external_derive)]
32. pub struct UserFrame {
33.     /// Frame address.
34.     addr: FrameAddress,
35. }
36. 
37. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
38. verus! {
39. 
40. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
41. use crate::mm::phys::FrameAllocView;
42. 
43. /// Abstract view of a user frame: the physical address of the owned frame.
44. impl View for UserFrame {
45.     type V = int;
46. 
47.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int {
48.         self.addr@
49.     }
50. }
51. 
52. /// Abstract view of the user page pool: the frame partition it draws from.
53. ///
54. /// `Upool` is `external_body` (its real state is the global frame allocator), so its view
55. /// is uninterpreted — the trust obligation is tracked by the type being `external_body`.
56. impl View for Upool {
57.     type V = FrameAllocView;
58. 
59.     uninterp spec fn view(&self) -> FrameAllocView;
60. }
61. 
62. } // verus!
63. 
64. #[verus_verify]
65. impl UserFrame {
66.     ///
67.     /// # Description
68.     ///
69.     /// Instantiates a user frame.
70.     ///
71.     /// # Parameters
72.     ///
73.     /// - `addr`: Frame address.
74.     ///
75.     /// # Returns
76.     ///
77.     /// A user frame.
78.     ///
79.     #[verus_spec(result =>
80.         requires
81.             addr.inv(),
82.         ensures
83.             result@ == addr@,
84.             result.inv(),
85.     )]
86.     pub fn new(addr: FrameAddress) -> Self {
87.         Self { addr }
88.     }
89. 
90.     ///
91.     /// # Description
92.     ///
93.     /// Returns the physical address of the target user frame.
94.     ///
95.     /// # Returns
96.     ///
97.     /// The physical address of the target user frame.
98.     ///
99.     #[verus_spec(result =>
100.         requires
101.             self.inv(),
102.         ensures
103.             result@ == self@,
104.             result.inv(),
105.     )]
106.     pub fn address(&self) -> FrameAddress {
107.         self.addr
108.     }
109. 
110.     ///
111.     /// # Description
112.     ///
113.     /// Consumes the user frame without freeing the underlying physical frame.
114.     ///
115.     /// # Returns
116.     ///
117.     /// The frame address.
118.     ///
119.     #[verus_spec(result =>
120.         requires
121.             self.inv(),
122.         ensures
123.             result@ == self@,
124.             result.inv(),
125.     )]
126.     pub fn leak(self) -> FrameAddress {
127.         let this: ManuallyDrop<Self> = ManuallyDrop::new(self);
128.         this.addr
129.     }
130. 
131.     ///
132.     /// # Description
133.     ///
134.     /// Adds a new reference to the underlying physical frame and returns a fresh
135.     /// [`UserFrame`] handle that owns that reference. The two handles share the
136.     /// same physical frame, and the frame is only reclaimed once both handles are
137.     /// dropped.
138.     ///
139.     /// This is the building block for copy-on-write sharing: the parent retains
140.     /// its handle, the child receives the returned handle.
141.     ///
142.     /// # Returns
143.     ///
144.     /// On success, a new [`UserFrame`] that aliases the same physical frame as
145.     /// `self`. On failure, an error is returned.
146.     ///
147.     #[verus_spec(result =>
148.         requires
149.             self.inv(),
150.         ensures
151.             match result {
152.                 Ok(uf) => {
153.                     &&& uf@ == self@
154.                     &&& uf.inv()
155.                     &&& crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(self@)
156.                 },
157.                 Err(_) => {
158.                     ||| !crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(self@)
159.                     ||| crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.refcounts[self@] >= 255
160.                 },
161.             },
162.     )]
163.     pub fn share(&self) -> Result<UserFrame, Error> {
164.         frame::share(self.addr)?;
165.         Ok(Self { addr: self.addr })
166.     }
167. 
168.     ///
169.     /// # Description
170.     ///
171.     /// Returns the current reference count of the underlying physical frame.
172.     ///
173.     /// # Returns
174.     ///
175.     /// Upon success, the current reference count of the underlying physical frame is returned.
176.     /// Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
177.     ///
178.     #[verus_spec(result =>
179.         requires
180.             self.inv(),
181.         ensures
182.             match result {
183.                 Ok(count) => {
184.                     &&& crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(self@)
185.                     &&& count as int == crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.refcounts[self@]
186.                 },
187.                 Err(_) => !crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(self@),
188.             },
189.     )]
190.     pub fn refcount(&self) -> Result<u8, Error> {
191.         frame::refcount(self.addr)
192.     }
193. }
194. 
195. #[verus_verify]
196. impl Drop for UserFrame {
197.     #[verus_spec(
198.         opens_invariants none
199.         no_unwind
200.     )]
201.     fn drop(&mut self) {
202.         if let Err(e) = frame::free(self.addr) {
203.             #[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]
204.             error!("failed to free user frame: {:?}", e);
205.         }
206.     }
207. }
208. 
209. //==================================================================================================
210. // User Frame Pool
211. //==================================================================================================
212. 
213. ///
214. /// # Description
215. ///
216. /// Thin facade over the module-level [`frame`](super::frame) allocator. Exists as a distinct type
217. /// so user-frame allocation has its own entry point ([`Upool::alloc`] returning [`UserFrame`]).
218. ///
219. #[derive(Debug)]
220. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
221. pub struct Upool {
222.     /// Private field prevents external construction.
223.     _private: (),
224. }
225. 
226. #[verus_verify]
227. impl Upool {
228.     ///
229.     /// # Description
230.     ///
231.     /// Instantiates a user frame pool.
232.     ///
233.     /// # Returns
234.     ///
235.     /// A user frame pool.
236.     ///
237.     // Dependency contract: opaque pool facade whose real backing store is the global frame
238.     // allocator. `external_body` (the `Upool` struct carries no spec-readable state) per
239.     // `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`. The pool introduces no frames of its own; `wf()` is the
240.     // only fact its boot-time caller needs before handing the pool to `PhysMemoryManager::init`.
241.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
242.     #[verus_spec(result =>
243.         ensures
244.             result@.wf(),
245.     )]
246.     pub(super) fn new() -> Self {
247.         Self { _private: () }
248.     }
249. 
250.     ///
251.     /// # Description
252.     ///
253.     /// Allocates a single user frame from the user frame pool.
254.     ///
255.     /// # Returns
256.     ///
257.     /// Upon success, a user frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
258.     ///
259.     // Dependency contract: delegates to the global frame allocator (`frame::alloc`). Modeled
260.     // as a watermark-agnostic single-frame allocation over the pool's frame partition. Marked
261.     // `external_body` until the `frame` free-function layer is verified.
262.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
263.     #[verus_spec(result =>
264.         requires
265.             old(self)@.wf(),
266.         ensures
267.             final(self)@.wf(),
268.             match result {
269.                 Ok(uf) => {
270.                     &&& old(self)@.free_frames.contains(uf@)
271.                     &&& final(self)@ == old(self)@.alloc_one(uf@)
272.                 },
273.                 Err(_) => {
274.                     &&& final(self)@ == old(self)@
275.                     &&& old(self)@.free_count() == 0
276.                 },
277.             },
278.     )]
279.     pub fn alloc(&mut self) -> Result<UserFrame, Error> {
280.         let addr: FrameAddress = frame::alloc()?;
281.         Ok(UserFrame::new(addr))
282.     }
283. }
284.

3. impl UserFrame {
4.     /// Well-formedness of a user-frame handle: its owned physical address is page aligned.
5.     ///
6.     /// This is purely structural; it makes **no** ownership claim (it does not assert the frame
7.     /// is allocated or has a positive refcount). Ownership is a per-operation transition fact,
8.     /// not a handle invariant, because `new` legitimately fabricates handles from
9.     /// PTE-recovered addresses (the probe / take-to-free / re-wrap idioms) without touching the
10.     /// frame partition. Surfaced so the refcount-affecting methods can discharge the frame
11.     /// layer's `frame.inv()` precondition.
12.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
13.         self@ % crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size() == 0
14.     }
15. }
16. 
17. } // verus!
18.
